item.html:
What is Standing Seam Metal Roofing?

When homeowners want a roof that they will likely never have to replace again, they turn to standing seam metal roofing. Unlike the exposed-fastener corrugated metal panels often seen on barns or sheds, a standing seam system is a premium architectural product. It consists of continuous metal panels (typically steel or aluminum) that run vertically from the ridge of the roof down to the eaves. The defining feature of a standing seam roof is the raised, interlocking seams that connect each panel.

These seams are elevated above the level of the roof deck, and all the fasteners are completely hidden underneath them.This concealed fastener design is crucial—it completely eliminates the risk of water penetrating through screw holes, which is the most common cause of leaks in cheaper metal roofs. The result is a sleek, modern aesthetic combined with a virtually impenetrable, weatherproof barrier that is tailor-made to handle the extreme weather volatility of Texas.

item.html: Frequently Asked Questions About Metal Roofs
item.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Metal Roofs

items.q: Are metal roofs noisy when it rains?
items.a: This is a common misconception! When installed over a solid wood roof deck, along with proper underlayment and attic insulation, a standing seam metal roof is no noisier during a rainstorm than a traditional asphalt shingle roof.

items.q: Will a metal roof attract lightning?
items.a: A metal roof does not increase the likelihood of your home being struck by lightning. In fact, if your home were to be struck, a metal roof is one of the safest materials you can have because it is non-combustible and will safely disperse the electrical charge.

items.q: Will a metal roof attract lightning?

items.q: Can you install a metal roof over my existing shingles?
items.a: While it is technically possible in some situations, Core Four Roofing generally recommends a full tear-off. Removing the old shingles allows us to inspect the underlying wood decking for hidden rot or damage, ensuring a flawless, long-lasting installation for your new metal system.
